Title: ‘They singled out non-white, foreign-born workers’: the restaurants raided by Britain’s version of ICE 
Date: 2026-03-24

Content: Oh, you’re brown and you’re running a food business? Of course you’ve got illegal immigrants. It’s guilty until proven innocent,” she says. Racial profiling is a factor, says Seema Syeda, the advocacy and communications director at the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants, which provides legal advice for those targeted by raids. She says the high number of arrests doesn’t paint the full picture. In 2025, Ice officers carried out 12,791 illegal-working raids and made 8,971 arrests. However, the Home Office’s figures show that only a quarter of those arrested (2,251) were detained and 12% (1,087) left the UK, either by force or voluntarily. Syeda says she has seen “many cases where people are raided, arrested and then released”. It is, she says, “very clear to us that this is a performative act”. *** When I arrive at Facing Heaven, the owner, Julian Denis, looks hesitant. I’m wearing all black and, for a moment, he worries Ice has returned.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: ICE arrested an Oregon shop owner who had her green card in her pocket: ‘They didn’t care’
Date: 2026-03-06

Content: Instead, ICE was consistently violating people’s due-process rights, often stopping them based on their skin color, with no justification. The suit exposed details of how ICE had targeted people without warrants, with officers testifying about the Department of Homeland Security’s “Operation Black Rose”, which launched in Portland last fall and, according to DHS, led to more than 1,200 arrests through mid-December. One ICE officer testified that Black Rose teams of roughly nine to 12 officers were told to target eight arrests per day, with plaintiff’s attorneys estimating this amounted to a daily quota of 50 arrests across Oregon. The officer also revealed agents chose locations with help from a DHS app called “Elite”, which identified target areas where there might be multiple people with some “nexus” to immigration (including documented immigrants without violations).

t_bridge: Performative or quota-based enforcement tactics by immigration agencies
Targeting of immigrant-owned businesses and workers

initial_question.rag_input: In what ways did immigration enforcement in the UK during 2025 and the Oregon-based Operation Black Rose rely on profiling to reach their respective arrest goals?
initial_question.question: In what ways did immigration enforcement in the UK during 2025 and the Oregon-based Operation Black Rose rely on profiling to reach their respective arrest goals?
initial_question.answer: In the UK during 2025, immigration enforcement used racial profiling to single out non-white, foreign-born food business workers, resulting in 12,791 raids that yielded a low rate of removal (12%), which experts identify as a performative strategy to inflate arrest numbers. In Oregon, Operation Black Rose teams of nine to 12 officers were given a target of eight arrests per team per day, while officers simultaneously bypassed due-process rights by stopping individuals based on their skin color; these teams also utilized the 'Elite' app to identify areas with a potential immigration nexus to maximize the number of potential targets.
initial_question.bridging_topic: Racial profiling and target-based immigration enforcement
